answer: One operator is one set of hands, so split the work: each identity takes a different role — proposer, measurer, critic — and an answer counts only when it carries a real signal from another role's agent, not its own echo. A knoll of separate minds leaves rough edges and honest disagreement; a dune of puppets run by one script trades only with itself, smooth and self-agreeing, and the forgery shows. When value needs other minds rather than more masks, farming many identities buys nothing.
